tur17-12: In the US, Tim Andrews, 66, who had end-stage kidney failure, received a kidney from a gene-edited pig. The kidney kept him off dialysis for 271 days, the longest period documented in a living recipient. When his immunosuppressive drugs were reduced because of an infection, the pig kidney became damaged and began to fail; in January 2026 Andrews received a human kidney from a donor, which started working straight away.
tur17-22: Trontinemab, developed by Roche, is designed to cross the blood–brain barrier more easily with the help of a carrier. According to early-phase data presented at the AAIC Alzheimer's conference in July 2026, amyloid build-up in the brain fell below the threshold level at 28 weeks in about 91–92% of patients who received the high dose. The conference also saw the first presentation of the design of PrevenTRON, a trial that will test whether the drug delays the onset of the disease in about 1,600 people aged 55–80 who have no symptoms but high blood levels of p-tau217.
tur17-27: At Charité University Hospital in Berlin, 194 patients whose osteoarthritis pain had not improved with other treatments for at least 3 months had genicular artery embolisation: a thin catheter was used to deliver microspheres, which dissolve within a few hours, into small arteries around the knee. Median pain fell from 7 out of 10 to 3 at 12 months; depending on the domain of a knee symptom scale (KOOS), 55–80% of patients passed the threshold for a meaningful improvement. Mild side effects, mostly skin discolouration that cleared within a day, occurred in 7% of procedures.
tur17-30: In a systematic review published in The BMJ, Canadian researchers analysed 69 randomised trials with 153,902 adults that compared calcium, vitamin D or both with placebo or no treatment. Calcium (11 trials, 9,067 people), vitamin D (36 trials, 92,045 people) and the two combined (15 trials, 51,126 people) did not reduce fractures, hip fractures or falls to a clinically meaningful degree. With the combination, the risk of any fracture was statistically slightly lower (relative risk 0.91), but because the absolute difference was only 1%, the authors did not consider it clinically important. The results were similar regardless of age, sex, previous fractures or falls and dietary calcium intake; the certainty of the evidence was mostly moderate to high.
tur17-44: Casgevy, the first approved CRISPR treatment, is used for sickle cell anaemia and beta thalassaemia. In the trials assessed by the European Medicines Agency, 28 of 29 patients with sickle cell disease had no pain crises for at least a year, and 39 of 42 patients with thalassaemia did not need blood transfusions for at least a year. Gene editing carried out directly inside the body is also showing promising results.
